note: Fifth sitting of locations.registry.ids-stay-here, from scratch, driving the adr-0014 worktree's bin/walkdown.js in a fresh mktemp tree with two scratch WALKDOWN_HOMEs and real git repos (a serve on 4799 only for ?bp=, killed after). The four earlier move failures (n-0378, n-0390, n-0391, n-0394 for both a committed home with a different-origin repo at the old path and a personal-only no-remote checkout named back with --project) all keep their IDs now. A new move case loses the ID: a committed home whose checkout is moved and whose same origin is cloned again at the old path. q-0384 (the claims cache holds IDs) is an open question on the wording and was not judged, though the cache is the only file outside registry.yml that holds an ID.

results.reasoning: Most THEN lines hold. acme_main and shop each get an ID of four digits, code and description (0001-am-search, 0002-sp-search). --blueprint takes the ID from anywhere and `search` alone inside each project. Threads, sweep run records, the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md pointer and the committed home hold no ID: a grep of every file outside registry.yml finds only cache/claims.json, which is q-0384 and not judged here. Commit spec and commit none change the home on 0002's row and keep the ID. A forgotten 0006 is followed by 0007. All four earlier move failures now keep their IDs: the n-0378 move, the n-0390 personal home with a remote, the n-0391 no-remote rename named back with `blueprints import . --project deli`, and the n-0394 case, where a new repository stands at the old path, for both a committed home and a personal one. A checkout mixing a committed and a personal blueprint also moves whole. The fourth THEN line still breaks in a new way: moving the checkout must change the path on the row and keep the ID. Setup: commit a home locally, `mv app app-old`, then `git clone` the same origin at $S/app (or git init there with the same remote). `blueprints import . --all` in app-old then says `listed ... as 0002-oa-search`, not `moved`. 0001-oa-search is left reading (gone), and the new row's checkout names $S/app, the fresh clone, not app-old. checkoutFor treats the moved tree as 'a clone of $S/app's origin' before register() can see the move. Forgetting the new row and importing with --project origin-app gives yet another new ID, 0003, so there is no way back. A secondary point: a serve started inside shop refuses ?bp=search with 409 'names 2 blueprints here', so ?bp= does not take the description alone inside a project the way --blueprint does.
